headline: Cisco Talos exposes how criminals now run Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini in their operations even as AI agents and chat logs spill developer secrets and wallet keys of their own.

emerging_trends.text: Cisco Talos pulled prompt logs straight off criminal endpoints running Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and Gemini, laying bare how routine cloud AI has become in offensive operations.
Attackers keep sidestepping authentication itself, extracting passkey private keys from Chrome's Google Password Manager as device-code phishing jumped 1,500 percent this year.
Ransomware crews keep turning perimeter appliances into entry points, with INC Ransomware racing to exploit SonicWall's SMA 1000 VPN flaws as fresh victims pile onto its leak site.

topics.title: Fresh Breaches Hit Hospital, U.K. Police, and River Bank
topics.latest_developments: An extortion group stole personal, financial, and medical data on 150,000 people from Madera Community Hospital in California, ExfilSquad leaked contact details of more than 100,000 officers and criminal-justice staff pulled from the U.K.'s Police National Legal Database, and River Bank said the crew behind its June ransomware attack deleted the data it took.
topics.summary: Three unrelated intrusions surfaced new victims across healthcare, law enforcement, and finance. Affected people should watch for identity theft and targeted phishing.

sources.title: 150,000 Impacted by Madera Community Hospital Data Breach
ExfilSquad hackers leak info of over 100,000 UK police officers, staff
River Bank Says Hackers Deleted Data Stolen in Ransomware Attack

topics.title: Adversaries Weaponize Commercial AI
topics.latest_developments: Cisco Talos published prompt logs it collected from compromised threat-actor endpoints running Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Cursor, and Gemini, documenting how attackers lean on cloud AI to write and debug their malware.
topics.summary: Talos gathered the logs off attacker machines, showing criminals now treat commercial coding assistants as standard tooling for building malware. Defenders fold the same platforms into their security operations centers to write detections and triage alerts.

sources.title: "Keep going, bro. You've got this!" A data-driven look at how adversaries are weaponizing AI
FOMO in the SOC: Where AI Platforms like Claude Actually Fit

topics.title: AI Agents and Chats Spill Secrets
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek detailed a Gemini agent-to-agent attack in which a crafted prompt to a low-privilege Google ADK agent passes a poisoned hand-off comment to a privileged agent, exposing secrets and tampering with pull requests, while Schneier flagged Claude conversations—some holding cryptocurrency wallet keys and home addresses—surfacing in Google search.
topics.summary: AI systems keep leaking the data users feed them. Google's ADK lets a low-privilege agent escalate through a privileged one, and a data-sharing toggle pushes private Claude chats into public search. Anthropic frames the chat exposure as a user-setting choice.

sources.title: Gemini Agent-to-Agent Attack Method Exposed Secrets, Enabled Pull Request Tampering
Some Claude Chats Are Searchable on Google

topics.title: Decades-Old BMC Flaw Exposes 24,000 Servers
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek reported a decades-old baseboard management controller vulnerability that leaves more than 24,000 internet-accessible server-management interfaces disclosing authentication hashes before login, putting thousands of data centers at risk.
topics.summary: The flaw leaks authentication hashes from server-management interfaces before any login, handing attackers a foothold into the underlying hardware. Operators should pull these interfaces off the public internet and lock down access.

sources.title: Decades-Old BMC Vulnerability Exposes Thousands of Data Centers to Attacks

topics.title: Pass-ta-key Attacks Hijack Google Passkeys
topics.latest_developments: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 disclosed three techniques—Pass-ta-key, Silver Pass-ta-key, and Golden Pass-ta-key—that let malware already running as an ordinary user on Windows abuse Chrome's Google Password Manager cloud authenticator to sign into passkey-protected accounts, bypass user verification, and pull passkey private keys.
topics.summary: Malware on a compromised Windows machine hijacks synced Google passkeys with no fingerprint, PIN, or on-screen prompt. The Golden Pass-ta-key variant steals the account master key and exports the private keys; anyone relying on Chrome's synced Google Password Manager passkeys faces the risk.

sources.title: New Pass-ta-key attacks let malware hijack Google-synced passkeys
Google Password Manager Attacks Could Let Malware Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts

topics.title: INC Ransomware Exploits SonicWall SMA 1000
topics.latest_developments: Resecurity named INC Ransomware the dominant actor exploiting the recently disclosed SonicWall Secure Mobile Access 1000-series VPN flaws, reporting that the crew accelerated its activity since early August 2026 and listed multiple fresh victims on its data-leak site.
topics.summary: INC Ransomware breaks into organizations through flaws in SonicWall's SMA 1000 VPN appliances, then steals data and extorts. Administrators running the SMA 1000 series should patch and hunt for signs of compromise.

sources.title: INC Ransomware Emerges as Dominant Actor Exploiting SonicWall SMA 1000 Flaws

business_politics.title: U.S. Intervenes to Prop Up the Yen
business_politics.latest_developments: Trump and Japan's finance minister both confirmed the two governments intervened jointly in currency markets, and the dollar fell sharply against the yen, in what the Financial Times calls a new era of American "currency activism."
business_politics.summary: The U.S. Treasury under Scott Bessent, working with Tokyo, sold dollars to buy yen to halt the Japanese currency's slide, a break from decades of American reticence on exchange rates; the coordinated action signals Washington will now move against trades that run counter to its interests, unsettling any bank running large dollar-yen positions.

sources.title: Bessent's yen intervention signals new era of US 'currency activism'
Yen intervention = US self-preservation

business.title: Pennsylvania Opens $10 Million Fund for Frozen Fruit Crops
business.latest_developments: State officials rolled out a new $10 million grant program to offset the fruit-crop losses an April deep freeze inflicted on Western Pennsylvania growers.
business.summary: A sudden April freeze devastated Western Pennsylvania's fruit crops, and Pennsylvania officials have launched a $10 million grant program to help farmers offset the damage.

sources.title: Pa. fruit farmers face crop losses after April freeze, turn to new $10M grant program

business.title: PixCams Trains AI on African Wildlife
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette profiled how the Pittsburgh-area company PixCams built round-the-clock camera and AI systems to track African wildlife and help spot poachers.
business.summary: PixCams, a Pittsburgh-area company, developed continuous camera and artificial-intelligence technology now used to monitor African wildlife, including black rhinos, and to help catch poachers.

sources.title: Pittsburgh-area company found a better way to track African wildlife 24/7

around_town.title: PennDOT Targets Parkway East "Bathtub" Flooding
around_town.latest_developments: PennDOT announced upgrades to the downtown Parkway East "bathtub" to curb the flooding that submerges the highway when the Monongahela River tops 25 feet.
around_town.summary: The low "bathtub" stretch of the Parkway East in downtown Pittsburgh floods whenever the Monongahela River rises above 25 feet, an increasingly frequent event, and PennDOT now plans drainage upgrades to keep the highway open.

sources.title: Upgrades coming to the Parkway East "bathtub" to help alleviate flooding concerns

around_town.title: ICE and a Data Center Split Springdale
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource published two investigations detailing how a year of ICE arrests and opposition to a proposed data center has turned Springdale into a civic battleground, and scrutinizing the borough's police chief.
around_town.summary: In Springdale, an Allegheny Valley borough of 3,000 east of Pittsburgh, a year of immigration arrests and opposition to a proposed data center has fueled a wave of civic organizing, and PublicSource reported the borough's police chief has drawn civil and criminal complaints across his career amid clashes with critics.

sources.title: How ICE and a data center turned a small Pittsburgh suburb into a civic battleground
ICE-allied police chief in Springdale faced lawsuits and allegations before clashes with critics

around_town.title: Dormont Fights High-Rise at T Station
around_town.latest_developments: Dormont residents pushed back against a proposed high-rise apartment building that would replace the park-and-ride lot beside the T station.
around_town.summary: A developer has proposed a high-rise apartment building on the park-and-ride lot next to Dormont's T station, and residents are objecting; borough leaders emphasize the project remains in its early stages.

sources.title: Dormont residents push back against proposed high-rise apartment project

events.latest_developments: Barrel and Flow, the Black-owned-brewing festival that USA Today readers rank among the country's best, returns Thursday, August 6 through Sunday, August 9 at multiple Pittsburgh locations.
events.summary: Barrel and Flow, an annual festival celebrating Black excellence in brewing, runs Thursday, August 6 through Sunday, August 9 at multiple Pittsburgh locations; details and tickets are at barrelandflow.com.

around_teams.title: Cherington Bets on the Bullpen, Holds the Rest
around_teams.latest_developments: General manager Ben Cherington explained his deadline haul, saying "we believe in the team," and left the Pirates' offense and starting rotation untouched even after Mitch Keller's season-ending injury.
around_teams.summary: The Pittsburgh Pirates rebuilt a battered bullpen at the August 3 deadline by adding Luke Weaver, Kirby Yates, and Lake Bachar, and the Post-Gazette's Noah Hiles argues the upgrades now leave the offense and rotation to carry a team clinging to contention.

sources.title: Ben Cherington revamps the Pirates' bullpen with a flurry of moves before the MLB trade deadline
Noah Hiles: Bullpen upgrades at the deadline put pressure on the Pirates to finish the job

around_teams.title: Can Kaleb Johnson Crack the Backfield in Year 2?
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette assessed whether running back Kaleb Johnson, who barely played as a rookie, can earn a role in the Steelers' backfield this season.
around_teams.summary: Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson never found his footing as a rookie, and the Post-Gazette weighs his chances of working into the offense under Aaron Rodgers and Mike McCarthy behind Jaylen Warren.

sources.title: Kaleb Johnson never found his footing as a rookie. Can he work his way into the Steelers' offense in Year 2?

around_teams.summary: Steelers receiver Roman Wilson is battling Germie Bernard for playing time behind Michael Pittman Jr. and DK Metcalf, and the Post-Gazette's Noah Hiles calls him the player with the most to gain this camp.
